title: Equipment Maintenance
description: Standard operating procedure for preventive maintenance, inspection, and repair of aquaculture equipment. Covers pump systems, filtration equipment, aeration systems, backup power, and monitoring equipment. Regular maintenance prevents catastrophic failures that can result in organism mortality.

steps.title: Electrical Safety
steps.description: Working with aquaculture equipment involves electrical hazards near water. Always disconnect power before servicing equipment. Use ground fault circuit interrupters (GFCI) on all outlets. Never operate electrical equipment with wet hands or while standing in water.
checklistItems: Confirm equipment is powered off before maintenance
Lock out/tag out electrical connections when required
Verify GFCI protection is functional
Keep hands dry when handling electrical components
Inspect power cords for damage before each use
Report any electrical hazards immediately

steps.title: Daily Equipment Visual Inspection
steps.description: Perform visual inspection of all critical equipment daily. Early detection of problems prevents equipment failure and organism loss.
checklistItems: All pumps running and producing expected flow
Air pumps and blowers functioning normally
No unusual sounds from motors or pumps
No water leaks at connections or fittings
Electrical panels dry and doors closed
Emergency equipment accessible and ready
Backup systems in standby mode
Alarm systems functional
Temperature control systems operating
All timers and controllers set correctly

steps.title: Pump Inspection and Maintenance
steps.description: Pumps are critical life support equipment. Inspect pump performance regularly by monitoring flow rates, listening for unusual sounds, and checking for vibration. Most pumps require impeller inspection and bearing lubrication on a scheduled basis.

steps.title: Weekly Pump Maintenance
steps.description: Perform weekly pump maintenance tasks to ensure reliable operation.
checklistItems: Check pump intake screens for debris buildup
Clean strainer baskets on all pumps
Verify pump priming (no air in lines)
Check mechanical seals for leaks
Listen for bearing noise or vibration
Verify flow rates match expected values
Check motor temperature (should not be hot to touch)
Inspect pump mounting and secure if loose
Document pump hours if meter installed

steps.title: Filter Maintenance Overview
steps.description: Filtration systems require regular maintenance to function properly. Mechanical filters need frequent cleaning. Biological filters require monitoring but minimal intervention. UV sterilizers need bulb replacement and quartz sleeve cleaning. Follow manufacturer schedules and observe system performance.

steps.title: Mechanical Filter Maintenance
steps.description: Clean mechanical filters regularly to maintain proper flow and water quality.
checklistItems: Check filter pressure gauge (clean when pressure rises 5-10 psi above clean)
Backwash sand filters according to schedule
Replace or clean cartridge filters
Inspect filter media for channeling or degradation
Clean filter housing and O-rings
Verify bypass valves are closed after maintenance
Document filter cleaning and media replacement
Rinse cleaned media with system water before returning to service

steps.title: Biological Filter Protection
steps.description: Biological filters contain beneficial bacteria essential for water quality. Never clean biological media with chlorinated water or allow it to dry out. Avoid disturbing biological media unnecessarily. If cleaning is required, rinse with system water only and return to service immediately.
checklistItems: NEVER use chlorinated water on biofilter media
Keep biofilter media wet at all times
Minimize disturbance to biofilter beds
Clean only 25-50% of media at one time
Monitor ammonia/nitrite after any biofilter maintenance
Document any biofilter cleaning or media replacement

steps.title: UV Sterilizer Maintenance
steps.description: UV sterilizers require regular maintenance to remain effective. Clean quartz sleeves monthly or when visibly fouled. Replace UV bulbs according to manufacturer schedule (typically annually) or when output drops below effective levels. Always disconnect power before servicing.
checklistItems: Disconnect power before any UV maintenance
Check UV output indicator if equipped
Clean quartz sleeve with appropriate cleaner
Inspect O-rings and seals for wear
Track bulb hours and replace on schedule
Verify proper flow rate through unit
Never look directly at UV light when energized

steps.title: Aeration System Maintenance
steps.description: Aeration provides critical dissolved oxygen. Inspect air pumps, blowers, diffusers, and airlines regularly. Air pumps require diaphragm replacement periodically. Diffusers become clogged and need cleaning or replacement. Airlines can develop leaks or blockages.

steps.title: Weekly Aeration System Check
steps.description: Inspect aeration components weekly to ensure adequate oxygen supply.
checklistItems: Air pump/blower running normally (listen for strain)
Check air filter on blower intake (clean/replace as needed)
Verify all diffusers producing fine bubbles
Inspect airlines for kinks, cracks, or blockages
Check airline connections are secure
Clean or replace clogged diffusers
Verify check valves preventing backflow
Test backup aeration can be activated quickly
Document any diffusers replaced or cleaned

steps.title: Backup System Testing
steps.description: Backup systems must be tested regularly to ensure they work when needed. A failed backup during an emergency results in catastrophic losses. Test generators, backup pumps, emergency aeration, and alarm systems according to schedule.
checklistItems: Generator tested under load monthly
Generator fuel level adequate
Automatic transfer switch tested
Backup pumps tested monthly
Emergency aeration tested monthly
Battery backup systems charged
Alarm notification system tested
Emergency contact list current
Document all backup system tests

steps.title: Generator Maintenance
steps.description: Backup generators require regular maintenance to ensure reliability. Check oil levels weekly. Run generator under load monthly for at least 30 minutes. Maintain fuel supply with stabilizer for extended storage. Service according to manufacturer schedule.
checklistItems: Check oil level and condition weekly
Verify coolant level (if applicable)
Inspect belts and hoses
Test battery and charging system
Run under load for 30+ minutes monthly
Check fuel level and add stabilizer
Clean air filter
Document run hours and service history

steps.title: Monthly Preventive Maintenance Schedule
steps.description: Complete comprehensive monthly maintenance to prevent equipment failures.
checklistItems: Inspect and clean all pump impellers
Lubricate pump and motor bearings as specified
Check belt tension on belt-driven equipment
Inspect all electrical connections for corrosion
Test all float switches and level sensors
Calibrate flow meters and sensors
Clean heat exchangers and cooling coils
Inspect valve operation and replace worn components
Test emergency shutoff systems
Review equipment logs for trending issues
Update maintenance records
Order replacement parts for upcoming needs

steps.title: Spare Parts Inventory
steps.description: Maintain adequate spare parts inventory to enable rapid repairs. Critical spares include pump impellers, motor capacitors, diaphragms, O-rings, fuses, and UV bulbs. Know lead times for replacement parts and order before stock is depleted.
checklistItems: Critical spare parts list maintained
Minimum stock levels defined
Inventory checked monthly
Parts organized and accessible
Supplier contacts current
Long lead-time items identified
Parts storage conditions appropriate

steps.title: Maintenance Documentation
steps.description: Thorough maintenance records enable predictive maintenance and troubleshooting. Document all maintenance activities, parts replaced, observations, and equipment hours. Review records periodically to identify patterns and optimize maintenance schedules.

steps.title: Maintenance Log Entry
steps.description: Complete maintenance log entry for all work performed.
checklistItems: Date and time documented
Equipment ID recorded
Work performed described
Parts replaced listed with part numbers
Equipment hours noted if applicable
Observations and findings documented
Technician name/initials recorded
Follow-up actions noted if needed
Entry added to digital maintenance system

steps.title: Emergency Equipment Failure Response
steps.description: If critical equipment fails, immediately assess impact on organism life support. Activate backup systems. Notify supervisor. Begin troubleshooting while monitoring organism welfare. Document timeline of failure and response.
checklistItems: Assess immediate risk to organisms
Activate appropriate backup systems
Notify supervisor immediately
Begin troubleshooting cause
Monitor water quality parameters
Implement manual backup procedures if needed
Document failure timeline
Prepare incident report
Conduct post-incident review
